Global insured losses
Hurricane Helene and Milton, the second highest severe convective storms (SCS) and 
large-scale urban floods were the main events driving global insured losses from natural 
disasters of USD 137 billion in 2024. Man-made disasters triggered an additional 
USD 9 billion losses.
Primary and secondary perils
Hurricane Helene and Milton brought the share of insured losses from so-called primary 
perils to roughly 41% in 2024, more than double the share in 2023 (19%).
